data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density similar vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Treated fields show a subpopulation of enlarged nuclei (~1-4% of nuclei, e.g. 2 very large flat cells central in f_e6098f2d0b57, nucleus ~2x DMSO median diameter, pale blue DAPI), not seen in DMSO f_a8be9aee1b01 where nuclei are uniform small ovals. Consistent with measured frac_large_nucleus z=6.92, value 0.014 vs 0.0.

Increased bi/multinucleate cells in treated: cells with 2-3 blue nuclei within one green (tubulin)/red (actin) cytoplasm (e.g. bottom-left and lower-central clusters in f_e6098f2d0b57, lower-left clusters in f_6f91279310a7). DMSO shows mostly mononucleate. Consistent with frac_multinucleate_proxy z=4.92, 0.30 vs 0.17.

Slightly smaller, less round, more irregular cells: treated cells have spiky actin-red edges and lower solidity, less circular outlines vs DMSO compact epithelioid patches. Consistent with cell_area z=-3.33 (3364 vs 3839), cell_roundness z=-3.76 (0.538 vs 0.562) and cell_solidity z=-3.03 (0.831 vs 0.85) and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-3.68 (4.31 vs 4.85) indicating reduced cytoplasm per nucleus.

Few bright condensed mitotic-like figures (white-yellow DAPI + green tubulin, 3-6 per treated field, e.g. right edge and bottom-central in f_6f91279310a7; right edge and bottom-central in f_e6098f2d0b57) vs 2-4 per DMSO field. Modest increase, consistent with frac_mitotic_like z=2.26 (0.043 vs 0.013) which is below strong threshold |z|>3.

No dramatic change in tubulin-green intensity/structure nor actin-red collapse at identical contrast: green remains diffuse cytoplasmic with perinuclear enrichment, red remains cortical/lamellipodial. No microtubule loss, bundling, or actin puncta/stars visible in composites.

notable_cells.why: very large flat cell(s) with enlarged pale blue nucleus, exemplifies large-nucleus phenotype
cell with 2-3 nuclei in shared cytoplasm, exemplifies multinucleate proxy

candidate_mechanisms.why: enlarged/polyploid nuclei + increased multinucleation + irregular shape with only modest mitotic increase is classic Aurora B failure of cytokinesis; no strong microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer or actin disruptor cytoskeletal phenotype visible in composite

report.uncertainty: composites only, no grayscale channels; tubulin mitotic spindle morphology (monopolar vs normal) cannot be resolved. Eg5 or other mitotic kinase could give similar large-nucleus/multinucleate phenotype, so Aurora is provisional

data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 13 observations; candidates: Eg5 inhibitors, Microtubule destabilizers, Microtubule stabilizers, Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Treated fields show many bright, round mitotic-like cells (condensed DNA white/pink in composite, intense tubulin) vs rare in DMSO. Strong change with identical contrast.
Agrees with measurements: frac_mitotic_like z=+12.09, 17.8% vs DMSO median 1.3%.
Tubulin (green) more heterogeneous/ high contrast: bright bundles in long thin protrusions and in mitotics vs more uniform diffuse green in DMSO.
Agrees with measurements: tub_glcm_contrast z=+9.64, 0.004 vs 0.001 DMSO.
F-actin (red) more variable/punctate, focal red dots at protrusion tips and around mitotics vs continuous peripheral cortical red in DMSO control sheets.
Agrees with measurements: act_std z=+9.19, 0.184 vs 0.106 and act_glcm_contrast z=+8.37, 0.003 vs 0.002.
Mean cell footprint markedly smaller and less spread; treated cells isolated/spindle-like vs large polygonal epithelial sheets in DMSO.
Agrees with measurements: cell_area z=-10.20, 2384 vs 3839 DMSO.
Cell shape more irregular/elongated with long thin processes, reduced roundness and solidity vs epithelioid DMSO.
Agrees with measurements: cell_roundness z=-11.39, 0.491 vs 0.562; cell_solidity z=-7.80, 0.801 vs 0.85.
DNA (blue) nuclei on average smaller/shorter axis; many compact condensed mitotic figures vs large oval interphase nuclei in DMSO.
Agrees with measurements: nuc_major_axis z=-7.79, 30.5 vs 36.4 DMSO.

Not represented in provided measurements: overall cell number/density per field appears lower in treated vs confluent DMSO control, and interphase microtubule protrusions are abnormally long and thin.

notable_cells.why: representative central cluster of elongated cells with bright mitotic figures
bright mitotic-like cells with condensed DNA and intense tubulin

candidate_mechanisms.why: Strong mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like +12z) with small/spindle interphase cells and monopolar-like bright mitoses, typical antimitotic Eg5 phenotype and high tubulin/actin texture contrast.
Alternative antimitotic with same measured profile: mitotic arrest, decreased cell area/roundness/solidity, increased tubulin contrast.
Also causes mitotic arrest and bundled high-contrast tubulin in protrusions/mitoses; cannot distinguish from destabilizer on composite alone.
Aurora inhibition also elevates mitotic-like fraction but usually increases nuclear size; nuc_major_axis here decreased, making it less likely.

report.uncertainty: Only composites at single concentration (6uM) without grayscale channel separation; can't resolve spindle polarity (monopolar vs multipolar) definitively to separate Eg5 from general microtubule agents. Actin changes are secondary to mitotic rounding.

data.critique:
**Verdict: Do not approve; request one free analysis.**

The 0.58 Aurora calibration is too high given the contradictions. Protocol NSC favors the runner-up: Cholesterol-lowering 2/4 with high per-well similarity (0.61-0.76 at 2 and 6 µM), while Aurora gets zero NSC votes. Low doses do show enlarged nuclei, but absolute fractions are tiny (1-2% vs 0 in DMSO) and the key discriminating dose, index 4 (0.6 µM, rep 1), rests on a single 61-cell well with elevated cell area/DNA but multinucleate proxy actually down and mitotic near zero. High doses reverse the morphology (small nuclei, strong mitotic-like fraction, rising tubulin contrast), which Eg5/microtubule hypotheses also explain. No phenotype read yet checks the weak dose-4 well.

**Step:** describe_phenotype on the already-acquired dose index 4, replicate 1 well (0.6 µM, w_6d94986897) at zero budget cost. Visually confirm or refute true enlarged polyploid nuclei, multinucleate cells, and tubulin/actin pattern where the segmentations are weakest, to adjudicate Aurora vs the runners-up.
data.requested_experiment: Describe the visual phenotype of the single well at dose index 4, replicate 1 (0.6 µM, well w_6d94986897), with grayscale nuclear, tubulin, and actin channels alongside the already-collected morphometric NSC features, and compare its population composition against the lower-dose wells at indices 3-5 and the high-dose wells at indices 6-7.

Mean cell footprint larger vs DMSO. DMSO: compact polygonal epithelial clusters with cell-cell contact. Treated: spread, stellate/triangular cells with broad cytoplasm, especially f_f267, and less contact. Qualitatively larger area.
Increased cell footprint matches measurement z-scores for cell morphology. No morph quantitative measurement beyond size/shape; visual assessment relies on red actin and green tubulin co-stains.
Elongated morphology with spreading correlates with larger cell_major_axis and higher eccentricity values reported.
Cell morphological changes consistent with cell_area z=+4.96 value 4547 vs 3839 DMSO in treated cells.
Observed elongation matches cell_eccentricity z=+3.57 value 0.795 vs 0.771 DMSO. No other shape descriptors provided for validation.
Eccentricity increase suggests treated cells are more spindle-like than DMSO polygonal cells.
cell_nuc_area_ratio increase (z=+3.6, 5.37 vs 4.85) reflects larger cytoplasm relative to nucleus; seen as expanded green/red cytoplasm rim around blue nuclei.
Visual cytoplasm-to-nucleus ratio appears shifted due to increased cell spreading rather than nuclear shrinkage in treated images.
Multinucleation not visibly increased in treated fields compared to DMSO control population.
Visual lack of excess multinucleates agrees with frac_multinucleate_proxy z=-1.89 (0.12 vs 0.17 median) - no increase, if anything slight decrease.

DNA - blue: nuclei mostly oval/mononucleate, similar number per cell cluster as DMSO. No widespread fragmentation, micronuclei, or mitotic rosettes resolved in composite at this resolution. One mitotic/debris very bright spot at bottom of f_ecf - isolated, not representative.

Large-nucleus phenotype subtle but present: 1-2 nuclei/field noticeably larger than DMSO median (e.g. lower-center large nucleus in f_ecf681, top cells in f_f267). Majority similar size. Overall distribution shifted to larger.
Rare large nuclei consistent with frac_large_nucleus z=+9.96 value 0.02 vs 0.0 DMSO - strong relative increase but absolute fraction still low (2%), matching visual rarity.

Integrated DNA intensity appears slightly higher in few large nuclei (brighter more saturated blue). Population median increase z=+3.52 value 504 vs 400 DMSO supported by visual but subtle due to composite contrast.
Nuclear shape/roundness - nuclei remain generally oval, smooth contour; no severe lobulation. If anything mild irregularity.
Mild decrease in roundness consistent with nuc_form_factor z=-2.01 (0.908 vs 0.917) - not strong (|z|<3) and not striking visually.

Beta-tubulin - green: retained diffuse cytoplasmic signal filling cell body in both treated and DMSO. No obvious global loss, diffuse hazy loss, or dense bundled stabilizer phenotype at composite resolution. Individual microtubule filaments not resolved; no clear monopolar/multipolar spindle arrays, no mitotic arrest cluster.
Tubulin signal appears brighter more extended only because cells are larger/spread. No microtubule-specific z-score in table to validate.
Not covered by measurements - no tubulin intensity/texture feature provided.

F-actin - red: cortical/peripheral staining at cell edges present in both treated and DMSO, with ruffled borders and stress-fiber-like edge enrichment. Not absent, fragmented, or punctate. No actin-disruptor-like rounding/loss.
Retains actin architecture with peripheral concentration; no gross actin disassembly or condensation seen in composites.
Not covered by measurements - no actin intensity feature provided.

Measurements show frac_large_nucleus z +10 and nuc_dna_integrated z+3.5 with increased cell area - classic endoreduplication/G2 phenotype. report.uncertainty: CONC 0.6uM only composites at 1024x819, no grayscale channels, microtubule/actin filaments not resolved, mitoses not countable. Morphology dominated by low-density spreading (eccentric cells in sparse field) which inflates area/eccentricity. No microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer, actin disruptor, or Eg5 monopolar spindle pattern seen. Visual evidence alone insufficient for definitive MoA - therefore top call is unknown with Aurora/DNA-related as weak hypothesis driven mainly by z-scores, not by striking image phenotype; need higher-res DAPI/Tubulin and mitotic counts to confirm.

data.note:
Reflection on s_3069b9414e (simvastatin):

Unblinded ground truth: simvastatin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (ChEMBL CHEMBL1064, PMID 30422514; PMID 28613690), BBBC021 'Cholesterol-lowering'. Protocol scoring correct — revised conclusion Cholesterol-lowering matched.

Learning: 4-dose profile was biphasic and confused visual prior. Low-mid doses (0.2-0.6 µM) showed enlarged/polyploid-like nuclei (frac_large_nucleus z+6.9 to +10, nuc_dna_integrated z+3.5, cell_area z+5.0 at 0.6 µM, 61 cells) that mimicked Aurora kinase inhibitor cytokinesis failure; high doses (2-6 µM) reversed to small nuclei, strong mitotic-like fraction (z+12 at 6 µM), reduced area and high tubulin/actin texture contrast, mimicking Eg5/microtubule antimitotics. NSC vote was actually correct: 2/4 wells nearest Cholesterol-lowering with high similarity 0.61-0.76 at 2 and 6 µM (mevinolin/lovastatin refs), vs initial Aurora visual bias.

Visual re-check of dose-4 confirmed rare large nuclei (absolute 2% vs 0% DMSO) but no multinucleate increase (proxy z -1.9) and low-density spreading artifact inflating area/eccentricity — weak support for Aurora/DNA damage.

Takeaway: trust NSC prior when high-dose morphology converges on cholesterol-lowering references despite low-dose polyploid mimicry; statin pleiotropy can produce cytoskeletal/G2-like changes secondary to isoprenoid depletion.

PubChem CID54454 confirmed simvastatin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound: simvastatin - HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (Cholesterol-lowering) PMID 30422514, PMID 28613690, PMID 32729746. Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree e23/e24. Protocol (NSC majority vote Ljosa et al. 2013) was correct: 2/4 votes Cholesterol-lowering with summed similarity 1.377; per-well nearest MoA w_4c68b3dbce 6 uM 0.763 and w_d8b83f4cfe 2 uM 0.614 e9/protocol. Scientist conclusion Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.58 e19 then p=0.42 e22 was wrong. scientist_correct false, protocol correct.

What the evidence got right:
- High-dose phenotype was Cholesterol-lowering signature. acquire_well e3 (6 uM, 297 cells): frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1 but cell_roundness z=-11.4, cell_area z=-10.2 and e7 (2 uM, 285 cells): cell_area z=-8.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-6.5. NSC correctly assigned both to Cholesterol-lowering with high similarity 0.76 and 0.61 (protocol). Dose-response e13 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 over 4 wells was the only significant dose trend, consistent with subtle tubulin texture change rather than strong Aurora polyploidy.
- compare_to_reference_atlas e6 and e9: NSC vote was Cholesterol-lowering 1/2 then 2/4, k-neighbour 3/10 Cholesterol-lowering / 3/10 Eg5 / 3/10 Actin disruptors. This split should have been weighted more heavily than the low-N morphometric outliers.
- The negative evidence in dose_response was informative but I discounted it: e15 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e16 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e10 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e11 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e17 nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 - all non-significant, contradicting a coherent Aurora-driven polyploidy/endoreduplication dose-response.

What misled me and why:
- Low-mid dose enlarged-nucleus signal e2 (0.2 uM, 245 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+6.9, frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+4.9) and e8 (0.6 uM, 61 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, cell_area z=+5.0, cell_major_axis z=+5.3). I treated high z-scores as strong Aurora evidence in hypothesis updates e18 Aurora 0.62 supported by e2/e4/e8/e10/e11/e12/e15/e16.
- Acquisition choice: I acquired only 4 wells (e1: 8 doses available, 4 wells left) spanning 0.2, 6, 2, 0.6 uM. The critical discriminating well e8 had only 61 cells measured - sparse field spreading inflates area and nucleus size. I initially misinterpreted this as polyploidy.
- describe_phenotype confirmation bias: e4 (2 fields) candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors; e5 (4 fields) lower density 13 observations still listing Aurora/Eg5/Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers. I weighted microscopist Aurora mentions over the NSC prior e6/e9 which had zero Aurora votes.
- I rationalized the high-dose reversal to small nuclei as "Eg5/microtubule confounder" in e18/e19 rationale ("low-mid doses show strong polyploid cytokinesis-failure phenotype most consistent with Aurora inhibition, outweighing high-dose shrunken mitotic confounder") instead of recognizing it as the expected Cholesterol-lowering high-dose morphology with mitotic-like rounding and actin/tubulin contrast increase e11/e13/e14.

What the review and second look clarified:
- Review verdict request_experiment correctly flagged calibration too high (0.58) given tiny absolute fractions (1-2% vs 0% in DMSO) and the single 61-cell well with multinucleate proxy actually down and mitotic near zero. The requested free describe_phenotype e20 on w_6d94986897 (0.6 uM) returned 26 observations, density lower, candidates Aurora, DNA damage, DNA replication - but I then recalibrated only to Aurora 0.42 e21, noting "rare large nuclei confirmed but weak (2% absolute), no multinucleation increase, spreading artifact" and "high-dose reversal to small nuclei + strong mitotic arrest favors Eg5/microtubule" e22. That was directionally right (downgrade) but still retained Aurora as top hypothesis and ignored that NSC already classified that well as DNA replication 0.229 not Aurora, and that protocol majority remained Cholesterol-lowering.
